key_insight: Adding in-situ Al2O3 particles during friction stir welding of AA2014-T6/AA5083-H111 improved joint strength and wear resistance, with the best wear performance at 9 wt.% Al2O3.
engineering_relevance: This shows that friction stir processing with particle reinforcement can simultaneously enhance mechanical and tribological behavior in dissimilar aluminium joints.
method: Machined a 45° single V-groove along the weld line and filled it with Al2O3 particles.
Applied three friction stir processing passes to improve flow and particle dispersion.
Compared reinforced and unreinforced joints using hardness, tensile, SEM/EDS, fracture, and wear tests.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 105 VHN in the stir zone, an 18% tensile improvement over the unreinforced joint, and the lowest wear rate at 9 wt.% Al2O3.
watch_item: Performance depends on achieving uniform particle dispersion during multi-pass processing, so inconsistent mixing could limit reproducibility in larger-scale welding.
paper_title: Analysis of tensile properties, fracture characteristics, and microstructural features in friction stir welding of dissimilar aluminium alloys reinforced with Al 2 O 3
